description: Decode with the engine's decoders. At code capacity, give `code` and a `syndrome` (the violated checks) or an `error` (the flipped qubits: its syndrome is taken and its residual judged, logical or not): matching (exact) and union_find for codes whose qubits sit in at most two checks; color for colour codes (restriction to matching on the three restricted lattices, lifted at each colour, completed below half the distance by an exact search); relay_bp for any code (it can stall on a degenerate error of a topological code, and then says it did not converge); search for the lightest error with the syndrome up to max_weight. At circuit level, give `memory` ({distance, rounds, p}: the rotated surface-code memory experiment), `circuit` (the circuit text: tags, Pauli-target observables and coordinates read) or `model` (detector error model text, decompositions with ^ read), with the fired `detectors` (the prediction: which observables flipped) or `shots` (sampled and decoded: the failure rate and its standard error): matching (exact), correlated (exact matching twice through the model's decomposed faults, the second answer kept only when the model's mechanisms explain it more cheaply), union_find, bp_osd, window (a sliding window: `window` {commit, buffer} rounds; every edge set below half the distance is corrected once the buffer is at least (d + 1)/2), or, on the model whole with its hyperedges, relay_bp (belief propagation with disordered memory, relayed leg to leg), bp_lsd (belief propagation, then clusters grown by its marginals and solved by elimination), mwpf (the minimum-weight parity factor with its dual bound: settled when the correction is proven a lightest explanation), astar (the lightest explanation by A* search; settled when exact) or osd_beam (ordered statistics searched by a beam along jittered orderings, ranked by belief propagation's calibrated trajectory; settled when belief propagation alone explained the syndrome, and the gap between the two lightest classes of observables it met given), each with `settings`. `bb` ({code, cycles, p, basis}) is a bivariate-bicycle memory at circuit level. `windows` ({commit, buffer, gap, threads} rounds) decodes with one of these or bp_osd in parallel windows: cores of `commit` rounds decoded with `buffer` rounds either side, the gaps between decoded after them, the same bits on any number of threads. Sealed with the service's key.

bb.description: A bivariate-bicycle memory at circuit level: the code (bb:72 to bb:288, gross), noisy cycles, the uniform circuit-level rate and the basis.

circuit.description: A noisy Clifford circuit in the circuit text.

code.description: A code by name: surface:D (the rotated surface code, odd D from 3 to 15), toric:L (2 to 12), steane, color:D (the triangular 6.6.6 colour code, odd D from 3 to 15), bb:72, bb:90, bb:108, bb:144 (or gross) or bb:288 (bivariate-bicycle codes); or {"family", "distance" | "size" | "n"}.

decoder.description: The decoder (default: matching, or color for a colour code, relay_bp for a bivariate-bicycle code).

max_weight.description: search: the heaviest error to try.

memory.description: The rotated surface-code memory experiment at circuit level.

model.description: A detector error model in its text.

settings.description: At circuit level, relay_bp, bp_lsd, mwpf, astar and osd_beam: the decoder's settings (relay_bp: gamma0, gamma_min, gamma_max, first_iterations, leg_iterations, legs, solutions, seed; bp_lsd: bp_iterations, scaling, order; mwpf: exhaustive, order; astar: max_nodes, beam; osd_beam: bp_iterations, ranking (trajectory, final or minimum), draws, jitter, window, beam, depth, patience, train_shots, train_rates, epochs, seed); each not given takes its default.

shots.description: Sample this many shots of the circuit and decode each.

window.description: window: rounds each window commits and the rounds after them it sees.

windows.description: Parallel windows for bp_osd and the decoders on the model whole (default 2, 2, 2 rounds, one thread): every detector needs a round (bb, or a third coordinate).

name: qec_decode

anyOf.description: An error-correction answer as every host gives it (engine::qec: qec_code, qec_decode, qec_threshold and qec_learn on both servers, wai-quantum qec, POST /v1/qec/*, the browser engine's qec call, the Studio and Python): the request, and the result sealed in a job's form. A code with its distance certificate (or a given certificate checked); a syndrome, an error or a circuit's detectors decoded, or shots sampled and decoded; logical failure rates over distances and physical rates; a detector error model's mechanism rates learned from detection events. A result names the engine that made it and this schema (engine and schema). docs/qec.md explains each.
A code: its checks and stabilizers, k, its layout, the decoders it takes, and its distance certificate (or a given one's check).

certificate.description: A code's distance certificate (quantum_distance): in each sector, a witness logical of the least weight found and every lighter support ruled out by an exhaustive search over connected supports, re-checkable node for node; the code's families hash, the search's bound, the symmetries checked and used, and its reading. Given back to qec_code, it is checked against the code.

distance.description: The distance, when both sectors settle it; null when the search stopped at its bound first.

families.description: BLAKE3 of the code's check families, in hex.

x.description: One sector: the least weight of a logical found, a witness of that weight, and the weight below which the search ruled every support out.

z.description: One sector: the least weight of a logical found, a witness of that weight, and the weight below which the search ruled every support out.

certificate.title: wai.quantum.distance/1

check.description: A given certificate's check: its witnesses, and the search run again.

engine.description: The engine that made the result: the wai-quantum crate's name and version.

receipt.description: A result's receipt: an Ed25519 signature, by the key it names, over digest = BLAKE3("wai:quantum-service-receipt\x02" ‖ len ‖ request ‖ len ‖ result), each of request and result in its RFC 8785 canonical text (the result without its receipt member), each length 8 bytes big-endian. Whatever members the request and the result hold are sealed, the result's engine and schema among them. The first receipts (no canon member, $defs/first) sealed their writer's compact text under the domain ending \x01; they still verify. wai/extensions/quantum-providers.md section 8.2 states the seal in full, and section 8.4 what a verifier checks.

canon.description: The canonical form the digest is taken over.

digest.description: The digest signed, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

key.description: The signing key, 32 bytes in lower-case hex.

signature.description: The signature, 64 bytes in lower-case hex.

time.description: When the receipt was issued and, where it states one, until when it is offered, by the signer's clock, in milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. Absent on a receipt that seals no time (one from a host with no clock, or sealed before receipts stated one). With it, the digest is taken under the domain ending \x03 and ends with len ‖ the canonical text of this member, so the time cannot be changed or taken off (section 8.2).

not_after_ms.description: The first moment the receipt is no longer offered: after issued_ms.
